papers.title: COACH-D 2.0: A Server for Template-based Modeling of Protein-ligand Interactions.
papers.abstract: Protein structure prediction has been transformed by AlphaFold2 and related systems; however, accurately modeling protein-ligand interactions remains a major challenge. Template-based prediction using homologous structures remains a powerful strategy. Here, we introduce COACH-D 2.0, a substantially enhanced template-based method for predicting protein-ligand binding sites. This upgrade features three key advances: (1) integration of multimeric templates from Q-BioLiP into our in-house library, (2) a new multimeric structure processing module enabling binding site prediction for protein complex
papers.summary: COACH-D 2.0 is an upgraded web server for predicting protein-ligand binding sites using template-based modeling. It improves upon its predecessor by incorporating multimeric templates from Q-BioLiP and adding a module for processing protein complexes, addressing a key challenge in protein-ligand interaction modeling.

papers.title: Decoding non-fullerene acceptors for organic solar cells: a theoretical structure-property-performance perspective.
papers.abstract: Organic solar cells (OSCs) have become promising next-generation photovoltaic technologies because of their flexibility, solution processability, and light weight. However, the use of traditional fullerene-based acceptors has been hampered by poor absorption, poor tunability, and energy losses that require the fabrication of sophisticated materials like non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs). The purpose of this review is to provide multi-faceted theoretical insight into the structure-property-performance relationship in NFAs with emphasis on how electronic structure, optical behavior, charge transpor
papers.summary: This review provides a theoretical perspective on the structure-property-performance relationships of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) for organic solar cells, focusing on how electronic structure, optical behavior, and charge transport properties influence device performance. It highlights the advantages of NFAs over traditional fullerene-based acceptors and offers insights for designing more efficient materials.

papers.title: Therapeutic potential of Echinocactus grusonii and its associated endophytic fungus Aspergillus oryzae in neuroprotection: in vitro and in silico investigations.
papers.abstract: The Golden Barrel Cactus (Echinocactus grusonii, syn. Kroenleinia grusonii), native to Mexico, is well known in horticulture but remains insufficiently studied with respect to its chemical composition. This study examined the chemical profile and neuroprotective potential of Echinocactus grusonii spines and its endophytic fungus, Aspergillus oryzae. The spines contained markedly higher levels of phenolics (293 mg gallic acid/g DW extract), flavonoids (132 mg quercetin/g DW extract), and alkaloids (14.5 mg atropine/g DW extract) compared to the stem. Untargeted metabolomics (UPLC-HRMS/MS) tenta
papers.summary: This study explores the neuroprotective potential of the Golden Barrel Cactus and its endophytic fungus, finding that the spines are rich in bioactive compounds like phenolics and flavonoids. Through in vitro assays and in silico analysis, the authors suggest these natural products may offer therapeutic benefits for neuroprotection, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction by atomic force microscopy imaging and template matching allows rapid structural-based validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image.
papers.abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is a versatile multi-modal imaging method frequently used for structural characterisation of biological surfaces at the nanoscale. However, AFM-based three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction has hitherto not been possible due to the tip-sample convolution artifact that distorts AFM images of individual molecules, and the disconnect between two-dimensional AFM images of surface deposited molecules and their three-dimensional structures. Here, three-dimensional single-particle analysis was developed for rapid structure-based validation of protein structures
papers.summary: This paper presents a new method for three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction using atomic force microscopy (AFM) combined with template matching, overcoming the tip-sample convolution artifact that previously limited AFM structural analysis. The approach enables rapid structural validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image, providing a fast and accessible alternative for protein structure verification.

papers.title: Design, synthesis and activity evaluation of tetrahydroisoquinoline-based programmed cell death ligand 1 inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Small molecule blockade of the programmed death receptor 1 (PD-1)/programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) pathway represents a promising approach for tumor immunotherapy. Based on the previously developed 3D-quantitative structure-activity relationship pharmacophore model for PD-L1 inhibitors, virtual screening followed by homogeneous time-resolved fluorescence (HTRF) activity testing identified the compound {1-[(biphenyl-4-yl)methyl]-7-methoxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinolin-6-yl}acetic acid methyl ester (Compound Y6) as a hit. Analysis of computational docking results of compound Y6 with PD-L1
papers.summary: This study describes the design and evaluation of tetrahydroisoquinoline-based small molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway for cancer immunotherapy. Using a pharmacophore model and virtual screening, the authors identified compound Y6 as a hit, which was validated by HTRF activity testing and computational docking with PD-L1.

papers.title: Pyrene-linked heterocyclic pyrazoles: Synthesis, antimicrobial screening, and in silico molecular insights.
papers.abstract: A library of structurally diverse pyrene-linked pyrazole derivatives was designed and synthesized, and their antimicrobial properties along with molecular interaction behavior were systematically investigated. The target compounds were efficiently prepared through a straightforward synthetic approach and fully characterized using standard spectroscopic techniques, confirming the formation of the desired heterocyclic framework. Biological evaluation against selected Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and fungal strains showed noticeable differences in activity across the series, indicating a strong
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis of a library of pyrene-linked pyrazole derivatives and evaluates their antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and fungal strains. The compounds showed varying activity, and molecular interaction studies provided insights into their potential mechanism of action.

papers.title: Isotopic Editing Unveils Ergosterol-Dependent Sugar Orientation Constraints That Stabilize Amphotericin B Channel Assemblies and May Contribute to Their Clustering.
papers.abstract: Amphotericin B (AmB) is the drug of choice for treating systemic fungal infections. Its selective toxicity is thought to arise from preferential binding to ergosterol in fungal membranes, which enables stable ion-permeable pores. The amino sugar mycosamine, attached to the AmB macrolide ring, has been proposed to mediate specific interactions with ergosterol; however, its orientation in membranes remains elusive, mainly because glycosidic-linkage conformations are difficult to analyze in lipid bilayers. Here we apply an isotopic editing strategylate-stage glycosylation combined with site-sele
papers.summary: This study uses isotopic editing to determine how the mycosamine sugar of amphotericin B orients in fungal membranes, revealing that ergosterol-dependent constraints on sugar orientation stabilize the drug's ion channel assemblies and may promote their clustering. This provides a mechanistic explanation for the selective toxicity of amphotericin B toward fungi.

papers.title: Development of the First YTHDC1 Degrader with Improved Antileukemia Activity.
papers.abstract: N6-Methyladenosine (m6A) represents the most prevalent internal RNA modification in eukaryotic mRNA, with YTHDC1 serving as a critical nuclear reader protein implicated in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although selective inhibitors of YTHDC1 have been reported, whether targeted degradation of YTHDC1 could achieve enhanced therapeutic efficacy remains unexplored. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of the first PROTAC molecule targeting YTHDC1, termed XY-2, which was developed based on the cocrystal structure of YTHDC1 bound to its known inhibitor. XY-2 efficiently induced proteas
papers.summary: This paper reports the first PROTAC degrader (XY-2) targeting the m6A reader protein YTHDC1, designed from a cocrystal structure with a known inhibitor. XY-2 induces proteasomal degradation of YTHDC1 and shows improved antileukemia activity compared to existing inhibitors, suggesting that targeted degradation may offer enhanced therapeutic efficacy in AML.

papers.title: A Ligand-Triggered Receptor Conformation Enables the Design of Selective Agonists for the Dopamine 3 Receptor (D3R) Using a Bitopic Strategy.
papers.abstract: While G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) represent the largest drug target family, designing subtype-selective molecules is still a challenge, especially to distinguish among closely related subtypes. One of the most challenging cases is the distinction between dopamine D2R and D3R, pivotal receptors in motor functions and cognition, and targets of Parkinson's disease treatments, schizophrenia, or substance use disorders. Attempts to design D3R-selective molecules with ligands binding toward the first transmembrane helix (the most sequence-diverse and conformationally flexible segment in GPCR
papers.summary: This study reveals a ligand-triggered conformational change in the dopamine 3 receptor (D3R) that enables the design of highly selective agonists using a bitopic strategy, overcoming the challenge of distinguishing D3R from the closely related D2R. The findings provide a new structural basis for developing subtype-selective GPCR drugs with potential therapeutic applications in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Design, structure-based optimization and antiviral evaluation of potent inhibitors for the macrodomain Mac1 of SARS-CoV-2.
papers.abstract: Enzymatically active macrodomains of (+)ss-RNA viruses mediate immune evasion by countering ADP-ribosylation and are therefore promising druggable targets. Here we report testing of ADP / ADP-ribose analogues for their ability to inhibit Mac1 of SARS-CoV-2, measurement of the affinity of active compounds and characterization of their binding mode by cocrystallization, uncovering critical molecular determinants of protein-ligand interaction. Key findings of the resulting structure-activity relationship (SAR) include that inhibitory potency is improved by either replacing the distal ribose of AD
papers.summary: This study identifies and optimizes small-molecule inhibitors targeting the macrodomain Mac1 of SARS-CoV-2, which is involved in immune evasion. Through structure-based design and co-crystallization, the authors reveal key molecular determinants of binding and develop potent compounds with antiviral activity, providing a promising starting point for COVID-19 therapeutics.

papers.title: [Enhancing the thermostability of Pseudoalteromonas sp. κ-carrageenase through computer-aided rational design].
papers.abstract: κ-carrageenan oligosaccharides hold broad application prospects in the food and pharmaceutical fields due to their excellent bioactivity. κ-carrageenase is a key enzyme for the industrial production of high-value carrageenan oligosaccharides, while the insufficient thermostability limits its application. The objective of this study is to rationally redesign the κ-carrageenase derived from Pseudoalteromonas through a computer-aided strategy, with the aim of constructing and screening enzyme variants exhibiting significantly enhanced thermostability. Discovery Studio 2019 was used for multi-site
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used computer-aided rational design to enhance the thermostability of κ-carrageenase from Pseudoalteromonas, a key enzyme for producing bioactive carrageenan oligosaccharides. By introducing targeted mutations, the authors successfully constructed enzyme variants with significantly improved thermostability, which could benefit industrial applications.

papers.title: Understanding Adsorption and Reactions at Aqueous Oxide Interfaces with Neural Network Potential Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Chemical processes at metal oxide-water interfaces are of central importance in geochemistry, biology, and energy technologies. A better understanding of these processes would allow us to make a significant step toward optimizing and controlling them, which could in turn lead to broader impacts. Computational modeling is indispensable to accomplishing this task because complexity and disorder often make it difficult to extract atomistic information from experiments. Balancing computational cost and accuracy, simulation schemes based on efficient machine learning representations of the potentia
papers.summary: This review discusses how neural network potential molecular dynamics simulations can be used to study adsorption and reactions at metal oxide-water interfaces, which are important in geochemistry, biology, and energy technologies. The authors highlight that these machine learning-based simulations offer a good balance between computational cost and accuracy, enabling atomistic insights that are difficult to obtain experimentally.

papers.title: Computational mapping of productive POI-E3 ligase conformations to guide de novo degrader design: application to WEE1 and PKMYT1 PROTACs.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy, yet rational degrader design remains challenged by the dynamic nature of protein of interest (POI)-E3 ligase interactions. While X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM provide valuable structural snapshots, they are insufficient for capturing the conformational heterogeneity underpinning efficient ubiquitination and degradation. Here, we present a unified computational workflow to systematically generate and evaluate POI-E3 ligase conformational states for CRBN- and VHL-mediated proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs). T
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational workflow to map productive POI-E3 ligase conformations for PROTAC design, applied to WEE1 and PKMYT1. It addresses the limitation of static structural methods by systematically generating and evaluating conformational states to guide de novo degrader design.

papers.title: Water-soluble β-strand peptidomimetics.
papers.abstract: Mediation of protein-protein interactions with molecules that bind strongly and selectively to one of the partners at the protein interface is a promising therapeutic strategy for myriad diseases. One such approach is the rational design of non-peptidic scaffolds that reproduce the display of amino acid side chains from one face of a secondary structural element. We have previously disclosed proof-of principle syntheses of β-strand mimetics composed of alternating (hetero)aromatic and cyclic urea units, conformationally preorganised through dipolar repulsion in organic solvents, that are in go
papers.summary: This paper describes the synthesis and evaluation of water-soluble β-strand peptidomimetics, which are designed to mimic protein secondary structures for therapeutic targeting of protein-protein interactions. The compounds are conformationally preorganized and show improved aqueous solubility, a key step toward their practical use in biological settings.

papers.title: Investigating the Therapeutic Mechanism of Ginkgo Biloba Extract in Alzheimer's Disease via Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms through which ginkgolides in Ginkgo biloba extract (GBE) may protect against Alzheimer's disease (AD).
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular docking to explore how ginkgolides from Ginkgo biloba extract might protect against Alzheimer's disease, identifying key targets and pathways. The findings suggest that ginkgolides may act through multiple mechanisms, potentially offering a multi-target therapeutic approach for AD.

papers.title: Quantitative correlation of spectroscopic signatures with ligand-protein interactions in anti-cancer drug Afinitor: an integrated experimental-computational study.
papers.abstract: A detailed molecular-level understanding of anticancer drugs is essential for improving therapeutic efficacy and guiding rational drug design. Everolimus (Afinitor), a clinically important inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, is widely used in cancer therapy; however, a quantitatively grounded relationship between its spectroscopic characteristics and ligand-protein interactions remains insufficiently explored. In this study, an integrated experimental-computational approach was employed, combining FT-IR spectroscopy, UV-Vis spectroscopy, and molecular docking simulat
papers.summary: This study integrates FT-IR and UV-Vis spectroscopy with molecular docking to quantitatively link the spectroscopic signatures of the anti-cancer drug everolimus (Afinitor) to its interactions with the mTOR pathway. The findings provide a molecular-level understanding that could aid in rational drug design and improve therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Atomistic Insights into Graphene Oxide Dot Interactions with Integrin αVβ3 from Microsecond Simulations.
papers.abstract: Graphene oxide (GO)-based nanomaterials functionalized with targeting ligands are promising platforms for selective cancer drug delivery. Among relevant targets, integrin αVβ3 is a highly overexpressed receptor in several solid tumors and is commonly targeted using cyclic Arg-Gly-Asp (cRGD) peptides. However, the molecular details governing the interaction between cRGD-functionalized GO dots and integrins remain poorly understood. In this work, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between integrin αVβ3 and a nanocarrier composed of a GO dot coated
papers.summary: This study uses microsecond-scale all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to reveal how graphene oxide (GO) dots functionalized with cyclic RGD peptides interact with integrin αVβ3, a key cancer target. The simulations provide atomistic details of the binding interface and dynamics, which could inform the design of more effective GO-based drug delivery systems.

papers.title: Repurposing FDA-Approved Drugs as Nav1.7 Channel Modulators: An Integrated Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.7 is a strongly validated target for the development of novel, non-opioid analgesics due to its genetic link to pain signaling. To accelerate the discovery of safe Nav1.7 modulators, this study outlines an integrated computational pipeline to repurpose FDA-approved drugs. A structurally complete model of the Nav1.7 central pore was generated via homology modeling from a high-resolution cryo-EM structure (PDB: 7W9K) to ensure a physically consistent model suitable for dynamic simulations. We conducted a structure-based virtual screening of 2296 FDA-approved
papers.summary: This study uses a computational pipeline combining homology modeling, virtual screening, and molecular dynamics to repurpose FDA-approved drugs as modulators of the Nav1.7 sodium channel, a validated target for non-opioid pain relief. The approach identified potential drug candidates that may be rapidly advanced to clinical testing for pain management.

papers.title: Ensemble Docking and Molecular Dynamics Indicate Dynamic Modulation of hnRNPA1 UP1 Interdomain Behavior by Natural Products.
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins exhibit substantial conformational plasticity that complicates structure-based ligand discovery and computational characterization. In this study, we applied an integrated computational approach combining high-throughput virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, ensemble docking, and interaction energy analysis to examine ligand binding and associated dynamic effects in the UP1 domain of hnRNPA1. Screening of 2847 phytochemicals followed by scaffold-diverse molecular dynamics evaluation identified three representative ligandsAmentoflavone, Ginkgetin, and Withanol
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational approach—high-throughput virtual screening, molecular dynamics, and ensemble docking—to identify three natural products (Amentoflavone, Ginkgetin, and Withanol) that bind to the UP1 domain of hnRNPA1 and modulate its interdomain dynamics. The findings highlight the conformational plasticity of RNA-binding proteins and suggest these compounds as potential leads for further investigation.

papers.title: Collision-based synthesis of diamond-graphite nanocomposites: computational investigation.
papers.abstract: Diamond-graphite nanocomposites have attracted significant attention due to their unusual structure, combining graphitic and diamond domains within a single material, as well as their promising electronic and mechanical properties. However, existing synthesis routes typically rely on poorly controlled high-pressure, high-temperature phase transitions, limiting the ability to "tune" the relative proportions of graphite and diamond. Here, we explored an alternative strategy that avoids bulk phase transformations and instead targets the formation of interfaces between pre-existing graphite and di
papers.summary: This computational study explores a new approach to synthesizing diamond-graphite nanocomposites by colliding pre-existing graphite and diamond domains, avoiding the poorly controlled high-pressure, high-temperature phase transitions used currently. The findings suggest that collision-based synthesis can form stable interfaces between the two phases, potentially enabling better tuning of the composite's properties.

papers.title: Flavonol tri- and tetraglycosides from Albizia guachapele Baker: isolation and biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Phytochemical investigation of the leaves of Albizia guachapele Baker (Fabaceae) led to the isolation and identification of two previously unreported kaempferol tetraglycosides, designated Guachapins A and B, together with ten known compounds. Their structures were established by interpretation of spectral data, including UV, ESI-MS, and NMR as kaempferol-3-O-β-d-glucopyranosyl-(1→4)-α-l-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→6)-O-[α-l-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→2)]-β-d-galactopyranoside, namely Guachapin A (3) and kaempferol-3-O-β-d-glucopyranosyl-[6-O-E-feruloyl]-(1→4)-α-l-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→6)-O-[α-l-rhamnopyranosyl-(
papers.summary: This study reports the isolation and structural characterization of two new flavonol tetraglycosides (Guachapins A and B) from the leaves of Albizia guachapele, along with ten known compounds, using spectroscopic methods. The compounds were evaluated for biological activity, contributing to the phytochemical knowledge of this plant species.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology Guided Drug Repurposing and Molecular Modeling Identify Sulfasalazine as a Potential OXA-23 β-Lactamase in Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii has become a major health concern, primarily driven by the dissemination of class D β-lactamases, particularly OXA-23, which compromise the efficacy of last-line β-lactam antibiotics. Drug repurposing combined with structure-based computational approaches provides a promising strategy for accelerating the discovery of novel therapeutic candidates against multidrug-resistant pathogens. This study aimed to identify FDA-approved non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) with potential inhibitory activity against OXA-23 β-lac
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular modeling to screen FDA-approved NSAIDs for potential inhibitors of the OXA-23 β-lactamase, which is a key driver of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii. The authors identify sulfasalazine as a promising candidate for drug repurposing against this multidrug-resistant pathogen.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Insights into Antibiotic Structure-Activity Relationships and Mechanisms of Action: A Review.
papers.abstract: This review examines recent quantum chemical methodologies applied to investigating antibiotic structure and mechanisms of action. The discussion is organised into three sections: (1) enzymatic hydrolysis of the β-lactam ring, (2) interactions of antibiotics with ribosomal subunits and enzyme active sites, and (3) complex formation with metal ions. Each section evaluates how quantum chemical approaches, particularly density functional theory (DFT) and hybrid QM/MM techniques, model molecular processes relevant to antibiotic function, including transition states, electron density analyses, and
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent quantum chemical studies, particularly density functional theory (DFT) and hybrid QM/MM methods, applied to antibiotic mechanisms, covering β-lactam ring hydrolysis, antibiotic interactions with ribosomes and enzymes, and metal-ion complexation. It highlights how these computational approaches provide detailed insights into transition states and electron density that inform structure-activity relationships and mechanisms of action.

papers.title: Surface electrostatic networks control hydrophobic core remodeling in a pH-dependent switching protein.
papers.abstract: Communication between protein surfaces and their buried cores is central to protein structure and function, yet this phenomenon remains challenging to predict and control at high resolution. Changes in the protonation of surface ionizable residues communicate with the hydrophobic core, for example, in diverse pH-dependent protein functions. Hisactophilin, a histidine-rich actin- and membrane-binding protein, provides a general model for exploring such communication as it exhibits a finely tuned pH-regulated myristoyl-switching function. Upon reversible proton binding, the myristoyl group shift
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how surface electrostatic networks, particularly protonation changes of histidine residues, communicate with the hydrophobic core to regulate the pH-dependent myristoyl-switching function of hisactophilin. The study reveals that surface charge changes trigger remodeling of the hydrophobic core, providing a high-resolution model for understanding how surface-to-core communication controls protein function.

papers.title: MInt-HDX: Leveraging Hydrogen-Deuterium Exchange Mass Spectrometry and Machine-Learning to Improve Protein-Ligand Docking.
papers.abstract: Understanding protein structural dynamics is central to elucidating biological function and guiding therapeutic discovery. Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) typically offers peptide-level, and sometimes residue-level, time-dependent insights into protein structure, conformational dynamics and/or ligand binding. Yet, translating HDX-MS data into atomic-resolution insights and deriving mechanistic understanding remains a key challenge. Integrative strategies which utilize HDX-MS to inform computational modeling or simulations, traditionally leverage HDX-MS data with physics-
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces MInt-HDX, a machine-learning approach that integrates hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) data into protein-ligand docking to improve prediction accuracy. By using HDX-MS-derived constraints, the method enhances the ranking of near-native docking poses, offering a new way to translate experimental dynamics data into atomic-resolution structural insights for drug discovery.

papers.title: CHARMM-GUI Covalent Ligand Docker as a Web-based Molecular Docking Platform for Covalent Ligands.
papers.abstract: Covalent inhibitor research is an emerging topic in drug discovery due to its superior performance in specificity and inhibition effects. While molecular docking is a popular strategy in prediction and assessment of ligand conformations or poses in receptor proteins, covalent ligand docking requires nontrivial preparation efforts, as the ligand structure changes during the covalent complex formation. In order to facilitate molecular docking for covalent ligands, we have developed CHARMM-GUI Covalent Ligand Docker (CGUI-CLD), a new module for covalent ligand docking supported by AutoDock4. CGUI
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces CHARMM-GUI Covalent Ligand Docker (CGUI-CLD), a new web-based platform that simplifies molecular docking for covalent inhibitors by automating the preparation of ligand and receptor structures for covalent complex formation. The module is built on AutoDock4 and aims to reduce the technical barriers and preparation efforts typically required for covalent docking studies.

papers.title: Ligand Design Using Unique Conformations to Preferentially Dock a Specific Site on Collagen-Bound MMP1.
papers.abstract: Precise site-specific ligand design remains a major challenge in structure-based drug discovery. Most existing approaches screen ligands against binding pockets identified from static protein structures obtained by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, or AlphaFold predictions. However, protein function is governed by a structure-dynamics-function relationship, and ligand screening that does not account for binding competition across the protein surface or the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent conformational states remains incomplete. Substrate-specific confo
papers.summary: This study presents a novel ligand design approach that leverages unique protein conformations to achieve site-specific docking on collagen-bound MMP1, addressing the limitations of static structure-based screening. By accounting for the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent states, the method improves selectivity for a particular binding site over competing surface regions.

papers.title: Structural Prediction and Functional Mechanistic Characterization of Farnesyl Diphosphate Synthase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis, triggered by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), continues to pose a major global health challenge, further intensified by the rise in drug resistance. The enzyme (2E,6E)-farnesyl diphosphate synthase (FPPS) in Mtb catalyzes the synthesis of farnesyl diphosphate (FPP), which is crucial for processes such as arabinogalactan biosynthesis in the cell wall. However, the functional characterization of Mtb FPPS is not well understood. Here, a hydrodynamic radius of 5.4 ± 0.3 nm was obtained for monomeric FPPS. The molecular docking relied on a structure predicted using Alph
papers.summary: This study provides structural and functional characterization of farnesyl diphosphate synthase (FPPS) from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, using a predicted structure and molecular docking to explore its catalytic mechanism. The authors report a hydrodynamic radius for the monomeric enzyme and highlight its role in arabinogalactan biosynthesis, offering a foundation for future drug design against tuberculosis.

papers.title: Computational Insights into PB1-F2 Mediated Modulation of VDAC1: An Allosteric Mechanism in Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
papers.abstract: The influenza-encoded virulence factor PB1-F2 has been implicated in a mitochondrial dysfunction of host immune cells through its interaction with the Voltage-Dependent Anion Channel 1 (VDAC1). This protein is a key outer mitochondrial membrane channel involved in ion and metabolite transport. Despite their well-known association, the precise interaction sites between these proteins remain unclear. In the current study, we employed multireplica all-atom molecular dynamics (MD), steered MD simulations, and docking approaches to investigate their mode of interaction. Our results reveal a putativ
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods (molecular dynamics, steered MD, and docking) to investigate how the influenza virulence factor PB1-F2 interacts with the mitochondrial channel VDAC1. The findings suggest a putative binding site and an allosteric mechanism by which PB1-F2 modulates VDAC1, potentially contributing to mitochondrial dysfunction in host immune cells.

papers.title: A Physically Informed QUBO Model for π‑Stacking Interactions in Molecular Docking Problems.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is a computational technique central to computer-aided drug discovery (CADD), aimed at predicting the preferred binding mode and binding affinity of a small-molecule ligand within the active site of a target macromolecule. Recent advances in quantum computing have led to the development of new molecular docking models. In particular, quantum annealing has motivated the formulation of physically informed docking frameworks that can be encoded within discrete optimization paradigms such as QUBO formulations.
papers.summary: This paper presents a new QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) model for molecular docking that incorporates physical information about π-stacking interactions. The model is designed to be compatible with quantum annealing, offering a potentially more accurate and physically realistic approach for predicting ligand binding modes in drug discovery.

papers.title: Effect of Relative Humidity on the Crack-Bridging Mechanism of CNTs at the CNT/C-S-H Interface.
papers.abstract: Carbon nanotubes-(CNTs) play a crucial role in enhancing the crack resistance of cementitious material, especially for mass concrete structures. However, the crack-bridging effect of CNTs remains unclear under different internal relative humidity (RH) conditions. In the present work, three-point bending experiments, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and theoretical analysis were systematically applied to investigate the crack-bridging effect of CNTs on cement composites. The results indicated that the crack-bridging effect of CNTs was highly dependent on RH and was primarily reflected by th
papers.summary: This study investigates how relative humidity affects the crack-bridging ability of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) in cement composites, using experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and theoretical analysis. The findings show that the crack-bridging effect is strongly dependent on humidity, with implications for improving crack resistance in concrete structures.

papers.title: Mapping of TEMPO‑, PROXYL‑, and Phosphoryl-Functionalized Spin Probes into Biointerface Fatty Acid Recognition Sites of BSA.
papers.abstract: A series of spin probes, bearing TEMPO, PROXYL or phosphorylated nitroxide paramagnetic groups attached to either terminal or internal position of an alkyl chain, are examined upon binding to bovine serum albumin, using an integrated spectroscopic, calorimetric, and computational approach. The structural diversity of spin probes allows a systematic investigation on how the type/position of paramagnetic moiety affect interaction. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and molecular docking reveal different dynamics of mid-chain and end-chain probes within distinct protein pockets. Mid-chain prob
papers.summary: This study uses EPR spectroscopy, calorimetry, and molecular docking to map how spin probes with different nitroxide groups (TEMPO, PROXYL, phosphoryl) and chain positions bind to bovine serum albumin. The findings reveal that mid-chain and end-chain probes occupy distinct protein pockets with different dynamics, providing insight into fatty acid recognition sites on BSA.

papers.title: DNA Binding Properties of Novel Pyrrolyl Quinones Derivatives: Insights from Spectroscopic, Electrophoretic and Computational Studies.
papers.abstract: In this work, we report the synthesis and Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)-binding properties of a new series of pyrrolyl quinone derivatives. These compounds were prepared from 2,5-dimethyl-1,4-benzoquinone through Michael-type addition/oxidation and electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions using pyrrole and bis-pyrrole nucleophiles. Additional structural diversification was achieved by reacting the pyrrolyl quinone intermediate either with 1-aminoanthracene or with acetone, affording new pyrrolyl quinone derivatives through distinct synthetic pathways. Owing to the electron-deficient π-conju
papers.summary: This study synthesizes a new series of pyrrolyl quinone derivatives and characterizes their DNA-binding properties using spectroscopic, electrophoretic, and computational methods. The compounds, prepared via Michael-type addition and electrophilic substitution, show promising interactions with DNA, providing insights into their potential as therapeutic agents.

papers.title: Protocol for Membrane Permeability Prediction of Cyclic Peptides Using Descriptors Obtained from Extended Ensemble Molecular Dynamics Simulations and Chemical Structures.
papers.abstract: Improving the membrane permeability is crucial in cyclic peptide drug discovery. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are widely used to analyze membrane permeability but are computationally expensive. Machine learning offers a low-cost alternative, but its performance is limited by the size of available experimental data sets and the difficulty of incorporating peptide-specific three-dimensional (3D) structural information. Although the 3D conformations of cyclic peptides are closely associated with membrane permeability, they are highly sensitive to subtle changes in the chemical structure. T
papers.summary: This protocol paper presents a machine learning approach for predicting the membrane permeability of cyclic peptides by combining chemical structure descriptors with conformational features from extended ensemble molecular dynamics simulations. It addresses the challenge of incorporating 3D structural information into ML models despite limited experimental data, offering a potentially more accurate and cost-effective alternative to pure MD-based permeability analysis for cyclic peptide drug discovery.

papers.title: Rational Design of Novel Isosteviol-Derived Factor Xa Inhibitors Using Integrated QSAR, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA Analyses.
papers.abstract: Factor Xa (FXa) remains an important target in the development of anticoagulant and antithrombotic agents. In this study, twenty isosteviol-derived oxime ether analogs previously reported as FXa inhibitors were used to develop a predictive QSAR model. The compounds were geometry-optimized at the B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) level, and Dragon molecular descriptors were calculated from the optimized structures. After descriptor filtering, Random Forest-based supervised preselection and correlation-based pruning were applied. Several models of increasing complexity were evaluated, including multiple linea
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods (QSAR, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA) to rationally design novel isosteviol-derived inhibitors of Factor Xa, a key anticoagulant target. By modeling 20 known analogs, the authors developed a predictive model and identified promising new compounds with improved predicted binding affinity and stability.

papers.title: Higher-order assembly of a type IX retron enables exploitation for designer antimicrobials.
papers.abstract: Bacterial defense systems provide a rich reservoir for biotechnological innovation. Retrons are tripartite abortive infection systems that detect phage invasion using reverse-transcribed DNA (msDNA), but how they structurally couple threat detection to effector activation remains poorly understood. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structure and activation mechanism of retron-Kva2, a type IX retron from the human pathogen Klebsiella variicola. We reveal that retron-Kva2 assembles into an asymmetric, higher-order ribonucleoprotein complex that sequesters a toxic dimeric HEPN RNase at its core. We
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports the cryo-EM structure of retron-Kva2, a type IX retron from Klebsiella variicola, revealing an asymmetric higher-order ribonucleoprotein complex that sequesters a toxic HEPN RNase dimer. The structural insights explain how threat detection is coupled to effector activation and enable the rational design of retron-based antimicrobials.

papers.title: Drying-Induced Structural and Oxidative Transformations in Sustainable Proteins: Impact on Physicochemical Properties and Flavor-Binding Functionality.
papers.abstract: The rapid global transition toward sustainable food systems has intensified interest in alternative protein ingredients derived from both terrestrial plants and blue foods. However, a critical bottleneck in the commercialization of these proteins is the stabilization of flavor profiles during dehydration. Drying technologies ranging from conventional hot-air and heat pump drying to microwave and vacuum freeze-drying inevitably induce structural reorganization and oxidative modifications. These transformations fundamentally modulate how volatile flavor compounds are bound, retained, and release
papers.summary: This review examines how different drying technologies (hot-air, heat pump, microwave, and vacuum freeze-drying) alter the structure and oxidation state of alternative proteins from plants and blue foods, and how these changes affect flavor-binding and release. The authors highlight that drying-induced structural reorganization and oxidative modifications are critical bottlenecks for stabilizing flavor profiles in sustainable protein ingredients.

papers.title: Structure-Based Screening of Antiviral Candidates Against Infectious Spleen and Kidney Necrosis Virus (ISKNV) Using Molecular Docking and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Infectious spleen and kidney necrosis virus (ISKNV) causes systemic infections and high mortality in various freshwater and marine fish species, posing a serious threat to aquaculture and ornamental fish industries. In this study, 72 antiviral compounds were screened against five ISKNV target proteins, DNA polymerase, transcription elongation factor (TFIIS), adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase), ankyrin repeat-containing protein, and major capsid protein (MCP) using molecular docking, followed by in vitro evaluation in dwarf gourami fin (DGF) cells. Fludarabine, liquiritin, and lycorine consisten
papers.summary: This study screened 72 antiviral compounds against five target proteins of infectious spleen and kidney necrosis virus (ISKNV) using molecular docking, identifying fludarabine, liquiritin, and lycorine as promising candidates. In vitro evaluation in dwarf gourami fin cells confirmed their antiviral activity, suggesting potential treatments for ISKNV infections in aquaculture.

papers.title: Targeting the RSV and hMPV L Protein: Cryo-EM and Structure-Based Approaches to Antiviral Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), members of the family Pneumoviridae, represent a foremost global cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection in infants, young children, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals. Despite the recent approval of preventive vaccines and monoclonal antibody prophylactics targeting the viral fusion protein, no widely adopted, RSV-specific direct-acting antiviral is currently approved for routine post-infection treatment. The large (L) protein of the viral RNA polymerase complex, which catalyzes genome replication and mRN
papers.summary: This review discusses the RSV and hMPV L protein as a promising target for antiviral drug development, highlighting recent cryo-EM structures and structure-based approaches. It emphasizes the urgent need for direct-acting antivirals against these respiratory viruses, given the limitations of current preventive measures.

papers.title: Tryptophan Residues' Incorporation Modulates Ferritin Thermal Stability and Hydrophobicity.
papers.abstract: Ferritin, a physiological iron-storage protein, has emerged as a highly attractive platform for drug delivery owing to its biocompatibility, structural robustness, and intrinsic ability to encapsulate and protect therapeutic cargo within its hollow nanocage. Building upon previous studies that established the baseline characteristics of engineered ferritin mutants in comparison to the wild-type protein, this work specifically investigates and directly compares the thermal stability profiles of two distinct mutated variants. These variants of human H-chain ferritin, obtained through targeted si
papers.summary: This study investigates how incorporating tryptophan residues into human H-chain ferritin affects its thermal stability and surface hydrophobicity, with implications for its use as a drug delivery nanocage. By comparing two engineered mutants to the wild-type protein, the authors provide insights into how specific amino acid changes can modulate the biophysical properties of this promising therapeutic carrier.

papers.title: Nanozymes in the Treatment of Pediatric Inflammatory Diseases: Opportunities and Challenges.
papers.abstract: Pediatric inflammatory diseases, such as neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), and asthma, pose numerous challenges in clinical treatment due to their complex pathogenesis and the still-developing stage of children's immune systems. These challenges include poor precision, strong toxic and side effects, and unclear long-term biological safety. In recent years, the development of nanozymes has provided new opportunities to address these issues. This review systematically summarizes the latest research progress of nanozymes in the diagnosis and treatment
papers.summary: This review discusses the potential of nanozymes—nanomaterials with enzyme-like activity—for treating pediatric inflammatory diseases such as necrotizing enterocolitis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and asthma. It highlights opportunities to improve treatment precision and reduce side effects, while also addressing challenges like unclear long-term safety. The paper provides a systematic overview of recent research progress in this emerging area.

papers.title: Integrating Molecular Similarity and AlphaFold-Based Structural Alignment for Target Discovery in Trypanosoma cruzi.
papers.abstract: Background: Chagas disease, caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, remains a major neglected tropical disease, with millions of people living with the infection worldwide. Current treatments are effective in the acute stage of the disease, but are poorly tolerated and show reduced efficacy in chronic infections, highlighting an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. A key bottleneck in early-stage drug discovery is target identification, which is traditionally dependent on costly and low-throughput experimental methods. Computational approaches offer a cost-effective and fast alterna
papers.summary: This study presents a computational pipeline that combines molecular similarity and AlphaFold-based structural alignment to identify potential drug targets in Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite causing Chagas disease. The approach offers a cost-effective alternative to experimental target identification, potentially accelerating early-stage drug discovery for this neglected tropical disease.

papers.title: Mechanical Regimes in Gelatin and Gellan Gum Bigels: Structure-Function Relationships and Dual Delivery of Carob Fruit Extracts.
papers.abstract: Bigels (BGs) were formulated using gelatin (GA) or gellan gum (GG) hydrogels (HGs) combined with beeswax-structured oleogels (OGs). Carob fruit extracts-an inositol-rich fraction (I-CFE) and a polyphenol-rich fraction (P-CFE)-were incorporated into the HG and OG phases, respectively, to enable dual delivery. The effects of composition on rheological, textural, thermal, color, and stability properties were evaluated at HG/OG ratios of 70/30, 60/40, and 50/50. GG-based BGs formed rigid, coherent, and crystal-reinforced networks, exhibiting the highest oscillatory stiffness and complex viscosity.
papers.summary: This study formulates bigels combining gelatin or gellan gum hydrogels with beeswax-structured oleogels, incorporating carob fruit extracts for dual delivery. Gellan gum-based bigels formed more rigid, crystal-reinforced networks with higher stiffness and viscosity, and the structure-function relationships were characterized across different hydrogel-to-oleogel ratios.

papers.title: Structural insights on the ligand selectivity of the mouse trace amine-associated receptor TAAR7e.
papers.abstract: Trace amine-associated receptors (TAARs), a G-protein-coupled receptor subclass detecting volatile amines, are co-expressed with odorant receptors in the main olfactory epithelium. While many behaviorally relevant amines are known for olfactory TAARs, the molecular basis of their selectivity for amines of varying lengths and primary/tertiary amines remains unclear. Using mTAAR7e as a model, we combined cAMP accumulation luciferase assays and computational simulations to investigate this issue. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and structure-activity relationship analysis established a clear
papers.summary: This study uses a combination of cAMP accumulation assays and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how the mouse trace amine-associated receptor TAAR7e achieves ligand selectivity for amines of different lengths and structures. The findings provide structural insights into the molecular basis of ligand recognition by olfactory TAARs, which are important for understanding how the olfactory system detects behaviorally relevant amines.

papers.title: Hierarchy of grammar rules for the language of transcriptional activation domains.
papers.abstract: Transcriptional activation domains (ADs) of eukaryotic gene activators have remained enigmatic for decades as short, consensus-less, extremely variable amino acid sequences that lack a specific structure and interact fuzzily with an uncertain number of targets. Understanding AD sequence grammar is critical for solving the enigma. Using rational design of AD sequences and high-throughput in vivo experimentation combined with bioinformatic analysis and machine learning, we refined grammar rules for AD sequences, calculated the relative importance of each rule to define a rule hierarchy, and link
papers.summary: This study decodes the sequence grammar of transcriptional activation domains (ADs), which are short, unstructured protein regions that activate gene expression. By combining rational design, high-throughput in vivo experiments, bioinformatics, and machine learning, the authors define a hierarchy of grammar rules and their relative importance, providing a predictive framework for AD function.

papers.title: RCSB protein data Bank: Next-generation advanced search for exploration of experimental structures and computed structure models.
papers.abstract: The Protein Data Bank (PDB), established in 1971, is the primary global, open-access archive for experimentally determined 3D macromolecular structures (proteins, RNA, DNA). The research-focused RCSB.org web-portal provides access to these data alongside more than one million machine-learning-predicted structure models, greatly expanding the available structural landscape. Rapid growth of both experimental and computational structures has increased the need for powerful yet accessible search tools that serve a broad and diverse scientific community. Herein, we describe a redesigned RCSB Protei
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: This paper describes a redesigned advanced search interface for the RCSB Protein Data Bank, which now integrates both experimental structures and over one million machine-learning-predicted structure models. The new search tools are designed to be powerful yet accessible, serving a broad scientific community by enabling more efficient exploration of the expanded structural landscape.

papers.title: Active components of Patrinia scabiosifolia and mechanisms of action against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus Epidermidis.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus epidermidis is a significant cause of hospital bloodstream infections, often transmitted through medical devices. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE) exhibits multidrug resistance, challenging clinical treatment. Current options are limited, with vancomycin as the primary choice despite its negative effects. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is a valuable resource for novel antibiotics; Our research showed Patrinia scabiosifolia has potent anti-MRSE activity. TCM's efficacy stems from active components, but active components and mechanisms of Patrinia scabio
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study identifies active components in the traditional Chinese medicine Patrinia scabiosifolia that show potent activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE), a common cause of hospital infections. The research reveals the mechanisms of action, offering a potential new source for antibiotics to combat multidrug-resistant bacteria.

papers.title: Druggable Mendelian randomization prioritizes CDH2 and supports finerenone as a candidate therapeutic strategy for diabetic retinopathy.
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy remains a major cause of vision loss, and therapeutic strategies beyond anti-vascular endothelial growth factor treatment are still needed. This study aimed to identify genetically supported druggable targets for diabetic retinopathy and to evaluate finerenone as a candidate therapeutic intervention in experimental retinopathy. We performed druggable Mendelian randomization by integrating druggable-gene resources, blood cis-expression quantitative trait locus data, and a large genome-wide association dataset for diabetic retinopathy. Significant genes were further evaluate
papers.summary: This study uses druggable Mendelian randomization to identify CDH2 as a genetically supported therapeutic target for diabetic retinopathy and provides experimental evidence that finerenone may be a promising candidate treatment. The findings highlight a potential new avenue beyond current anti-VEGF therapies.

papers.title: Computational Study of Terahertz-Induced Phase Transitions at Molecular Interfaces.
papers.abstract: Structural phase transitions driven by atomic rearrangements at the interaction interfaces of biological macromolecules, particularly proteins, are fundamental to regulating critical physiological processes, making their effective modulation key to developing targeted therapeutics. Existing induction strategies encounter substantial limitations: Chemical methods have difficulty accessing shallow binding pockets and can lead to invasive, irreversible modifications, while common visible and near-infrared modulation technologies are hindered by side effects induced by exogenous agents and restric
papers.summary: This computational study explores the use of terahertz (THz) radiation to induce phase transitions at molecular interfaces, particularly in proteins, as a novel non-invasive approach for modulating biological processes. The authors propose that THz stimulation can overcome limitations of chemical and optical methods, potentially offering a targeted strategy for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Theta-Defensin Proteins: Conformational Variability and Environmental Effects.
papers.abstract: Theta-defensins are a unique class of cyclic antimicrobial peptides known for their exceptional structural stability and broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. Despite their therapeutic potential in mammals, the effects of solvent environments and specific mutations on their conformational stability remain poorly understood. This paper employs all-atom molecular dynamics simulations under different solvent conditions to investigate the structural dynamics of baboon theta-defensin-2 (BTD-2) peptides, as well as solvent effects. BTD-2 was selected due to its higher arginine content, enhancing it
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to explore how solvent conditions and mutations affect the conformational stability of baboon theta-defensin-2 (BTD-2), a cyclic antimicrobial peptide. The findings reveal that environmental factors significantly influence the peptide's structural dynamics, providing insights that could inform therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven identification of DLL3 as a molecular target and development of a DLL3-binding cyclic peptide for glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains the most aggressive primary brain tumor and is associated with a dismal prognosis despite maximal multimodal therapy. Targeted radionuclide therapy requires a tumor-selective, cell-surface-accessible molecular target that is highly expressed in GBM but minimally present in normal brain tissue.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify DLL3 as a promising cell-surface target for glioblastoma (GBM) therapy, given its high expression in tumors and low presence in normal brain. The authors then develop a DLL3-binding cyclic peptide, providing a potential new avenue for targeted radionuclide therapy in this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Bisphenol A exposure in myasthenia gravis: Potential targets and mechanisms revealed by network toxicology and molecular dynamics.
papers.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a B-cell-mediated autoimmune disease characterized by impaired neuromuscular transmission. Although genetic predisposition and thymic abnormalities are well recognized, they cannot fully explain the increasing incidence and regional heterogeneity of MG, highlighting the potential contribution of environmental factors. Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, exhibits estrogenic activity, immunomodulatory effects, and mitochondrial toxicity, and has been implicated in multiple autoimmune disorders. However, the potential role of BPA in MG pathogen
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how Bisphenol A (BPA) exposure might contribute to myasthenia gravis (MG) pathogenesis. The authors identify potential molecular targets and mechanisms linking BPA to MG, suggesting that environmental factors like BPA could play a role in the disease's increasing incidence and regional variability.

papers.title: Design of a novel epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine against dengue virus: An immunoinformatic approach.
papers.abstract: Dengue imposes a profound global impact, with millions affected annually. Its transmission by Aedes mosquitoes poses significant challenges to combat, aggravated by urbanization and climate change. Despite efforts, no impeccable antiviral treatment exists to date, highlighting the urgency for a vaccine. Developing one encounters hurdles like the four distinctive serotypes of the virus and complex immune responses. In this study, we employed an immunoinformatics approach to design an epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine aimed at confronting all DENV serotypes. The study contemplates epitop
papers.summary: This study uses immunoinformatics to design a tetravalent subunit vaccine against all four dengue virus serotypes by selecting conserved epitopes. The approach aims to overcome challenges of serotype diversity and complex immune responses, offering a potential vaccine candidate.

papers.title: Structural and functional dissection of neutralisation differences among SARS-CoV-2 variants using antigenicity prediction and CR3022 binding analysis.
papers.abstract: Progressive waves of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) have been driven by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) variants carrying mutations in the spike glycoprotein, particularly in immunodominant regions such as the receptor-binding domain (RBD) and the N-terminal domain (NTD). These mutations can alter antigenic surfaces and are associated with changes in antibody recognition and vaccine-induced protection. Integrating experimental neutralisation data with computational analyses may contextualise variant-associated differences in antibody responses.
papers.summary: This study integrates experimental neutralization data with computational antigenicity prediction and CR3022 binding analysis to dissect how mutations in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein across variants alter antibody recognition. The findings provide structural and functional insights into variant-specific differences in neutralization, which may inform vaccine and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Transcriptomic analysis-driven identification and transcriptional characterization of Komagataella phaffii promoters from highly transcribed endogenous genes across diverse culture conditions.
papers.abstract: The yeast Komagataella phaffii (formerly Pichia pastoris) is a robust host for recombinant protein production, capable of growing at high cell densities, performing post-translational modifications, and efficiently secreting heterologous proteins. However, gene expression still relies mainly on the methanol-inducible AOX1 promoter (PAOX1) and the constitutive GAPDH promoter (PGAP), highlighting the need for alternative promoters with distinct regulatory properties. This study aimed to identify and characterize promoters from the most highly transcribed endogenous genes across diverse culture c
papers.summary: This study used transcriptomic analysis to identify and characterize new promoters from highly expressed endogenous genes in Komagataella phaffii, offering alternatives to the commonly used AOX1 and GAP promoters. The findings provide a set of promoters with distinct regulatory properties that could improve recombinant protein production under various culture conditions.

papers.title: Structural Modeling of Protein-DNA Interactions Underlying Genome Copy Number Variation in Nanoviruses.
papers.abstract: Multipartite nanoviruses possess multiple segmented genomes that accumulate at unequal levels during infection, giving rise to dynamic genome formulas. Although the replication of all segments relies on a common replication-associated protein (Rep), the molecular basis underlying segment-specific differences in genome abundance remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether protein-DNA interactions at conserved cis-regulatory elements are associated with this variability by focusing on the intergenic region (IR) of segment S of milk vetch dwarf virus (MDV). We used a structure-based
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling to investigate how protein-DNA interactions at conserved cis-regulatory elements may explain unequal genome segment accumulation in multipartite nanoviruses. Focusing on the intergenic region of milk vetch dwarf virus segment S, the authors explore whether Rep binding differences underlie segment-specific genome copy number variation. The work provides a structural perspective on a poorly understood aspect of nanovirus biology.

papers.title: The Interaction between the Tyrosine Kinase Receptor EphA2 and RNF5: Structural Insights from an In Silico Approach.
papers.abstract: EphA2 is a tyrosine kinase receptor from the Eph (erythropoietin-producing hepatocellular) family that is involved in several processes associated with regular cellular functions, as well as in different pathological conditions including cancer. EphA2 is up-regulated in many types of tumors, and the process of ligand-triggered receptor endocytosis and the subsequent degradation attract a lot of attention as a means of reducing receptor levels and its pro-oncogenic outcomes. In this context, the intracellular Sam (sterile alpha motif) domain of EphA2 (EphA2-Sam) plays an important role, being t
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to investigate how the tyrosine kinase receptor EphA2 interacts with the E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF5, focusing on the structural details of the EphA2 Sam domain. The findings provide insights into the molecular basis of EphA2 regulation, which could inform strategies to reduce EphA2 levels in cancer.

papers.title: AAV capsid sites breakdown: large protein insertions impact on vector dynamics.
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are one of the most used gene delivery systems, and several capsid engineering strategies have been followed to further improve their performance. Current capsid design approaches predominantly rely on small peptide insertions (<100 a.a.). Integrating large proteins poses challenges due to the nature of protein folding and the complexity of capsid assembly.
papers.summary: This review examines how large protein insertions into the AAV capsid affect vector dynamics, highlighting the challenges of maintaining capsid assembly and function when incorporating proteins larger than 100 amino acids. It provides a breakdown of capsid insertion sites and discusses implications for future capsid engineering strategies.
